Subject: Private deployment questionnaire — partitioned airlock details requested

Hi Ava,

Thanks for taking our inquiry. Attached is Aurora's standard Private Deployment Questionnaire (spreadsheet) — we've highlighted sections that are mission-critical for our compliance board: operator access controls, patch/patch-signing workflow, SBOM provenance, KMS integration, and telemetry egress controls for an air-gapped/partitioned deployment.

Two asks up front:
- Can you confirm if Redwood supports a multi-segment airlock topology where the control plane is on a dedicated management network and inference nodes reside on an isolated compute VLAN with unidirectional egress through an airlock appliance?
- Please include one or two examples of operator access flows (procedural + technical), whether operators require bastion jump hosts, and the KMS/HSM integration pattern for customer-managed keys.

Target timeline: we are consolidating responses for our security review on 2026-04-22. A single-package reply (PDF + attachments) would be ideal. If you need an NDA or data-processing addendum signed before sharing technical artifacts, let us know.

Appreciate it — Sasha

Sasha Patel

Hi Sasha — thanks for sending this over. We're happy to respond. I'll own the packet and coordinate internal artifacts. High-level answers below, and we'll follow up with a compiled package before your 4/22 deadline.

Quick answers:
- Yes — Redwood supports a partitioned airlock topology. We commonly deploy a separate management/control plane in a VPC segment that has one-way, customer-controlled egress via an airlock appliance to a staging zone; inference nodes run in isolated subnets without direct outbound internet access.
- Operator access: we support role-based operator accounts with MFA, optional bastion/jump host, ephemeral session tokens, and time-boxed escalation for emergency maintenance. KMS: integration patterns include customer-managed KMS (Cloud KMS / HSM) with envelope encryption for model blobs and secrets.

Action items (internal):
- Irene: produce a network diagram and short runbook covering operator access and bastion flows.
- Connor: collect SBOM export and signing verification steps.
- Marissa: prepare evidence checklist for telemetry/exfiltration controls and sample log scrubbing rules.

I'll attach an initial diagram and a short runbook draft later today.

Thanks,

On Thu, Apr 15, 2026 at 09:12 AM Sasha Patel <sasha.patel@aurora-healthtech.com> wrote:
> Thanks for taking our inquiry. Attached is Aurora's standard Private Deployment Questionnaire...

Ava / Sasha — attaching the diagram and a short operator access runbook as requested. Highlights and clarifications:

- Topology: The attached PDF shows three segments: Management (control plane), Staging (airlock appliance sits here), and Production (isolated inference subnets). The airlock appliance enforces unidirectional transfer of signed model artifacts and approved telemetry bundles.
- Operator access flow:
  1) Operators authenticate to customer's IdP (SAML/OIDC) and request an ephemeral session token via the bastion service.
  2) The bastion performs JIT approval (MFA + short-lived cert) and issues a 1-hour session with recorded keystroke/session logging (if customer enables auditing).
  3) For maintenance requiring model pushes, operators must sign artifacts locally; Redwood validates signatures against customer-managed key identifiers in the KMS before deployment.
- Patching and SBOM: We ship signed patches for runtime components. SBOMs are provided quarterly and on-demand; the attached sbom-summary.csv contains component names, versions, and source checksums. Verify signatures using our published public key; full SBOM (cyclonedx) is available under NDA/secure link.
- Telemetry: Default behavior is zero outbound telemetry from production inference subnets. Customers can opt-in to forward sanitized metrics via the airlock after explicit approval; unstructured logs are sanitized at source.

Notes: we can produce an operator playbook that ties these steps to the questionnaire rows if that helps your compliance team.

Attachments included: partitioned-airlock-nw-diagram.pdf, operator-access-runbook.md, sbom-summary.csv

— Irene Choi

Hi Sasha — thanks, and yes we can confirm the two points:

1) Airlock filtering: the appliance supports strict allowlisting by destination (IP/CIDR and FQDN) and content inspection by MIME/type and signature header. The airlock only permits artifact transfer when the signature header and artifact hash match a pre-authorized allowlist entry. We will include the airlock config snippet and sample ip/fqdn allowlist in the package.

2) SBOM verification keys: Redwood publishes a package signing public key that we exchange in the initial secure handoff. For customer-managed signing we accept certificates issued by the customer's KMS/HSM; verification is performed against the customer's public key fingerprint recorded in the deployment manifest. We'll provide fingerprint exchange guidance and an example key-rotation policy.

Attachments in this package (zipped):
- partitioned-airlock-nw-diagram.pdf (topology)
- operator-access-runbook.md (procedures + example bastion commands)
- sbom-summary.csv (component list & checksums)
- airlock-config-snippet.txt (allowlist + MIME filters example)
- deployment-manifest-template.yaml (key fingerprints + control-plane endpoints)

We also created a HubSpot record for the RFP (link below) and scheduled a technical review call with J. Morales on 2026-04-19 10:00 AM PT. If you want an NDA in place before we upload a full cyclonedx SBOM, we can route that to legal.

HubSpot link: https://hubspot.example/record/AH-2026-PVT-042

I'll follow up with Marissa to include the telemetry sample redaction rules. Let us know if you'd prefer a different time for the call.

Regards,
